chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“A man washes his hand once after sleep, twice after defecation and urination, and three times after janabah.”
So if he were to put his hand into the vessel before washing it, the water would not be spoiled, if the hand were pure; this indicates that.

key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep, after which the hand is washed once
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urination, after which the hand is washed twice
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: major ritual impurity requiring ghusl, after which the hand is washed three times
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation, after which the hand is washed twice
key_terms.طَاهِرَةً: ritually pure, meaning free from impurity

ai.seo_question: How many times should the hand be washed after sleep, relieving oneself, and janabah, and does putting an unwashed but pure hand into water spoil it?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed number of hand washings in different states: once after sleep, twice after defecation and urination, and three times after janabah. It also indicates that if a pure hand is placed into a vessel before washing, the water does not become invalidated.
